items.title: Alice Springs baby dies after mother forced to live with DV perpetrators

children.content: A six-week-old Aboriginal baby died after her mother was evicted and forced to sleep on the floor of an overcrowded house with people who had previously assaulted her, a coroner has found.

items.title: 'Grossly inadequate': NT traditional owners plan to mandate mine rehabilitation

children.content: Traditional owners in the NT want to see more money put aside for the rehabilitation of closed mines and are considering making it a requirement of any agreement established between mine companies and traditional owners.

items.title: Darwin hospital opens new ward with hopes of easing capacity pressures

children.content: A new multi-purpose ward at the Northern Territory's largest hospital has received its first patients this week, with hopes the $24 million investment will help ease capacity pressures in Darwin's health sector.

image.altText: A patient resting in a hospital bed, a health worker is standing next to her and looking at a health monitoring screen nearby.

items.title: Tourists survive 'scary' buffalo attack on popular NT hiking trail

children.content: Two young tourists say they've never been more scared in their lives after 21-year-old Victorian woman Emma Hipwell was charged by a wild buffalo while holidaying in the Northern Territory.

image.altText: Emma Hipwell lifts her shorts to show a number of large bruises on her right hip.

items.title: 'No-one told us anything': NT community without services months after floods

children.content: Months after record flooding, the remote Aboriginal community of Nauiyu / Daly River remains significantly damaged and without key services. Locals say some are still without power and little has been done to prepare for the next wet season.

image.altText: A group of white roof homes right on the bank of a large green river, with trees surrounding it.

items.title: Dugong population drops 50pc in 'real shock' for researchers

children.content: The number of dugongs in the Gulf of Carpentaria, one of the animal's most globally important populations, has halved in the past two decades, a decline scientists have called a "real shock".
